description: Probably Not(e) Arabic is a probabilistic quantiser built on Arabic maqams, each of which is made from one or more jins, with the notes tuned to the intervals those ajnas use.

params.text: Sets how many notes either side of the quantised note can be chosen; at 0 the quantised note is the only candidate.
An attenuverter, -100% to +100%, scaling the voltage at the input it belongs with before that voltage is added to the control's own setting.
Sets the direction of the choice: fully left only notes below the quantised note, centre both directions, fully right only notes above.
Sets the starting probability across the candidates: at 100% every candidate is equally likely, at 0% the furthest candidate falls to a tenth of the chance, rising linearly towards the centre.
Chooses the maqam within the chosen family; the list of maqams changes with the family.
Chooses the family the maqam comes from, which is its root jins, one of sixteen.
Treats the maqam as a scale with octave equivalence when lit; unlit, the whole sayr and its modulation routes are used and the input is limited to -1 to 1V, below 0V taking notes under the tonic.
Chooses the next jins at once, by weighted probability among the ajnas that are switched on.
Sets the tonic the maqam is played from, limited to the pitches that are realistic for that maqam.
Shifts the quantised note by whole octaves, -4 to +4.
Detunes the chosen note by a random amount of as much as 10 cents.
Draws the pitch randomisation from a Gaussian distribution when lit, from an even one when unlit.
Puts the current maqam's ajnas and their weights back to the values it ships with.
Puts the note weights of the current jins back to the values it ships with.
Bends the jins weights from linear fully left to logarithmic fully right, which widens the gap between likely and unlikely ajnas.
Bends the note weights from linear fully left to logarithmic fully right, which widens the gap between likely and unlikely notes.
Chooses which jins of the maqam's sayr the notes are taken from at the moment.
Takes that jins out of the modulation choices or puts it back.
Sets the probability weight of that jins when the next jins is chosen, 0 to 100%.
Takes that note of the current jins out of the choices or puts it back.
Sets the probability weight of that note within the current jins, 0 to 100%.
Sets the chance that the note last played is barred from being chosen again; at 100% a note never repeats.

inputs.text: The pitch to be quantised; in sayr mode it is limited to -1 to 1V, where negative voltages ask for notes below the tonic.
Voltage here is added to the setting of the control it belongs with, scaled by that control's attenuverter.
Voltage here moves through the maqams of the current family, 0-10V spanning the list.
Voltage here moves through the sixteen families, 0-10V spanning them all.
Voltage here moves the tonic through the pitches the maqam allows, 0-10V spanning them.
Voltage here shifts the output by octaves, 10V giving four octaves at a full attenuverter.
A trigger here chooses a new note; with nothing patched here no new note is chosen.
Takes the random number behind the note choice from this voltage, 0-10V, instead of the module's own.
Takes the random number behind the jins choice from this voltage, 0-10V, instead of the module's own.
A trigger here chooses the next jins by weighted probability among the ajnas that are switched on.
The voltage here picks the jins directly, one volt per jins counted from the first.
Adds to the weight of that jins, 0-10V covering the full range of the weight.
Adds to the weight of that note, 0-10V covering the full range of the weight.

outputs.text: The chosen note as pitch, tuned to the intervals of the current jins and including any pitch randomness.
The probability weight of the note last chosen, 0-10V.
A 10V trigger each time the chosen note differs from the one before.
The number of the jins in use, one volt per jins counted from the first.

notes: the quantised output does not move until a trigger arrives at the trigger input; each trigger is what picks the next note.
menu: Quantize Mode — how the incoming pitch is made to fit: Closet for the nearest note, Round Lower for down, Round Upper for up. Closet is the maker's spelling of closest.
Trigger Delay — holds the trigger by five samples, for clocks that arrive before the pitch has settled.

inputs.11: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.15: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
